Blepharitis can lead to other eye problems, including:
- Stye. A stye is a red, painful bump on the eyelid caused by a blocked oil gland.

- Damage to the cornea. In severe cases, blepharitis can hurt your cornea (the clear outer layer at the front of your eye). This can happen because of swelling or irritation in your eyelids or eye lashes that grow in the wrong direction.
- Chronic (long-term) red eye. Blepharitis can make the white part of your eye look red all the time [nei_007_chunk_04].

Eye doctors can check for Retinitis Pigmentosa (RP) as part of a comprehensive dilated eye exam [nei_020_chunk_03]. The exam involves eye drops to dilate the pupil, followed by a visual field test to check peripheral vision [nei_020_chunk_03]. Other tests include electroretinography (ERG) to check how well the retina responds to light [nei_020_chunk_03], optical coherence tomography (OCT) to take a detailed picture of the retina [nei_020_chunk_03], and fundus autofluorescence (FAF) imaging [nei_020_chunk_03]. Genetic testing is also used to learn more about the type of RP [nei_020_chunk_03].

This is general education, not a diagnosis.
